_note: HAND-WORKED by the author of contract 1.1.0 (Admin Phase 49), not run by any program in either app and not reviewed by anyone else. Every expected value follows engines.md section 27 by reading. If a fixture and the spec disagree, the spec wins and the fixture is a patch release.
how_to_read: L, B, S are chunk fingerprints (`content_sha256`; here shortened names). EMPTY = the chunk has zero rows locally (tombstones count as rows). MISSING = no such chunk (local: never written; server: no manifest row). rowsL / rowsB = row counts including tombstones, used only by S1. A case with no rowsL is not subject to S1.
decision_order: 2 L EMPTY or MISSING and S exists -> RESTORE
3 S MISSING and L has rows -> PUSH_ALL (then S1)
4 B absent and both have data -> MERGE_NEVER_OVERWRITE (then S1 on the push half)
5 matrix: L!=B & S==B -> PUSH; L==B & S!=B -> PULL_MERGE; both changed -> MERGE_THEN_PUSH
S1 applies to every outcome that ends in a push: if rows to be pushed < 0.7 x rowsB (strictly) -> STOP_OFFER_RESTORE

cases.why: local changed, server same as base
server changed, local same as base
local missing, never synced (no base), server has data
no base (never synced), both have data, different bytes
no base, both have data, same bytes
S1: local lost 40% of base rows, server equals base, local changed
S1 boundary: local lost exactly 30% (7 of 10) is NOT more than 30%
deleting is not shrinking: 10 of 10 rows still present, 4 of them now tombstones (tombstones count as rows), so S1 does not fire
S1 also guards the push half of MERGE_THEN_PUSH: merged result has 6 of base 10
local empty, server missing, base had data: nothing to push, nothing to restore
